title: Weekly Markets Monitor - Out of the ordinary
gist: World Gold Council: September saw gold fall more than 8% despite 70t+ of ETF inflows, an unprecedented combination, explained by COMEX managed-money and spread position unwinds, as weak US jobs and stable PCE trimmed rate-hike expectations.

insights.claim: Gold fell more than 8% in September (93rd percentile monthly decline) while global gold ETFs took in over 70t (77th percentile of inflows), a combination not previously observed since 2004.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Price weakness was driven by futures positioning, not ETF investors.

insights.claim: COMEX Managed Money positions fell by 84t equivalents and Spreading positions by 156t, explaining the price drop despite strong ETF demand.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Futures de-risking can dominate price in the short term; ETF buyers diverge from speculators.

insights.claim: A weaker-than-expected US jobs report and stable PCE inflation reduced expectations of near-term Fed rate hikes, while Eurozone and Tokyo inflation accelerated, China announced growth-support measures and the RBA raised rates.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Global tightening bias outside the US persists; rate-hike pricing is in play.

insights.claim: Bond yields and the US dollar rose last week while oil prices eased and equities were mixed.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Rising dollar and yields are a headwind for gold.
